2608.20918.title: UpgradeBench: A Decision-Centric Benchmark for Upgrading Fine-Tuned LLM Specialists
2608.20918.paper_summary: Organizations maintain task-specific adapters for open-weight language models, and each new base-model release forces a migration decision: retain existing specialists, port adapters, refresh from preserved behavior, or retrain. Prior transfer work evaluates isolated model pairs, without studying these choices across real model release sequences. We present UpgradeBench, a decision-driven longitudinal benchmark covering four consecutive Qwen releases, one continuation checkpoint, six tasks, and two model sizes, augmented by OLMo checkpoints with known training lineage. The benchmark disentangles three core questions: whether a new checkpoint improves fixed-recipe retrained specialist performance, whether specialization assets transfer across versions, and what recovery resources are usable. We observe upgrade gains differ across task-scale-release episodes: some retrained baselines improve while others stay within training noise, with durability ranging from under one release interval for text-to-SQL to over fourteen months for intent classification. Direct adapter copying depends neither on architecture nor model family: on OLMo, retention drops from 0.88-0.99 at 46B-token continued pretraining to zero at 2.9T tokens; annealing and model souping introduce no extra harm, with portability decaying with continued-pretraining distance. Given preserved input data, teacher relabeling recovers target-base specialists without fresh gold annotations, though compute savings are not guaranteed. Simulating a fixed decision policy over 33 upgrade episodes yields 0.37pp mean quality regret with zero behavioral regressions at one-third the compute and label cost of full retraining. A lightweight CKA probe over 256 prompts predicts cross-version adapter portability (Spearman 0.74 across eight model pairs). We release per-example predictions, cost logs, split manifests, and evaluation code.
2608.20918.paper_summary_zh: 組織為開放權重語言模型維護特定任務的適配器，每次新的基礎模型發布都迫使進行遷移決策：保留現有專家、移植適配器、從保留的行為中刷新或重新訓練。先前的轉移工作評估了孤立的模型對，而未研究這些選擇在實際模型發布序列中的情況。我們提出了UpgradeBench，一個以決策為驅動的縱向基準，涵蓋四個連續的Qwen發布、一個延續檢查點、六個任務和兩個模型大小，並通過具有已知訓練來源的OLMo檢查點進行增強。該基準解開了三個核心問題：新的檢查點是否改善固定配方重新訓練專家的表現、專業資產是否能跨版本轉移，以及可用的恢復資源是什麼。我們觀察到升級收益在任務-規模-發布事件之間有所不同：一些重新訓練的基線有所改善，而其他則保持在訓練噪聲範圍內，持久性從文本到SQL的不到一個發布間隔到意圖分類的超過十四個月不等。直接適配器複製既不依賴於架構也不依賴於模型家族：在OLMo上，保留率從46B-token的持續預訓練的0.88-0.99下降到2.9T tokens時的零；退火和模型湯不會引入額外的傷害，便攜性隨著持續預訓練距離的增加而衰減。在保留的輸入數據下，教師重新標記在沒有新的金標註的情況下恢復目標基礎專家，儘管計算節省並不保證。對33次升級事件進行固定決策政策的模擬，產生了0.37pp的平均質量後悔，且在全量重新訓練的三分之一計算和標籤成本下，沒有行為回退。一個輕量級的CKA探針在256個提示上預測了跨版本適配器的可攜性（Spearman 0.74，涵蓋八對模型）。我們發布了每個示例的預測、成本日誌、拆分清單和評估代碼。
